ideas.title: Due diligence consultants can security-audit an acquisition target's code entirely on one laptop
ideas.connection: Flint runs fast on a Mac via Rapid-MLX, Graphify gives it an auditable map of the codebase, and Cloudflare's audit skill turns that into verified, machine-readable findings, all without code leaving the machine.

ideas.title: Teams can prototype on cheap MiniMax API then self-host the identical model
ideas.connection: M3.1 Flash was available as a cheap 1M-context API, and now its open weights serve on SGLang, so a product can move in-house without changing models.

ideas.title: Enterprises can shift Claude workloads to whichever cloud has unspent committed budget
ideas.connection: Claude is now generally available under Google Cloud IAM and billing while already offered on Bedrock with structured outputs, so the same workload can be billed against either cloud commit.

ideas.title: Defense and government contractors can run code agents on air-gapped laptops with inspectable context
ideas.connection: Flint provides a laptop-class open coding model, Graphify gives it local repo context with explained edges, and OpenCode supplies the open agent loop, so the whole stack runs with no network calls.

ideas.title: Insurers can run legacy code war rooms on local models instead of token budgets
ideas.connection: GEICO's talk frames $1,000 a day in tokens for legacy code work, and an MIT-licensed local coding model plus a deterministic code knowledge graph could do much of that work in-house.

ideas.title: Open source maintainers can triage agent-found vulnerabilities locally before disclosure deadlines
ideas.connection: Patch the Planet signals a coming flood of agent-found bugs, Graphify maps the blast radius of each one with explained edges, and Sage-A1.5 runs the triage agent cheaply on modest hardware without sharing undisclosed bugs.

ideas.title: Platform teams can fund, prune and resell internal agent skills using named usage data
ideas.connection: Copilot metrics now show usage of each custom skill by name, and the Agent Skills standard moving to a foundation makes those skills a safer long-term investment across tools.

ideas.title: Inference resellers can quote open MoE serving on TPU capacity, not only GPUs
ideas.connection: TorchTPU lets existing SGLang serving code run on TPUs, and Beam 1.0 is a speed-focused open MoE that teams can download and run, so one serving stack can now be priced on two kinds of hardware.

ideas.title: SaaS vendors can turn agent security audits into ready compliance evidence trails
ideas.connection: Verified machine-readable audit findings, a hard human-approval gate, and agent config kept as reviewed YAML together produce the who-checked-what record auditors ask for.

ideas.title: Consultants can pilot DeepSeek on a Mac in a law firm, then scale unchanged
ideas.connection: Rapid-MLX makes a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash quant usable on one M3 Ultra for a private pilot, and DeepInfer lets the same DeepSeek model family run at production scale with DeepSeek's own serving framework.
